What Maternal Support Network does for you

🚑 Emergency response

One touch alerts an ambulance or community transport, your midwife, the nearest health worker, and your family — with your live location.

⏱️ Labour monitoring

A real contraction timer that tells you, in plain language, when it's time to leave for the facility — and warns on danger signs.

💰 Financial preparedness

A simple birth-savings plan, SHA/Linda Mama guidance, and links to SACCOs, chamas and maternal grants so cost never delays care.

⚠️ Maternal Support Network supports — it does not replace — a doctor, nurse or midwife. In any emergency, contact a skilled health provider immediately. Figures shown are illustrative for this prototype.

Emergency & transport coordination

Emergency Help

Maternal Support Network tackles the deadly "three delays": deciding to seek care, reaching a facility, and receiving care on arrival. One activation reaches everyone who can help — built on the m-mama community-transport model now backed by Kenya's Ministry of Health.

Activate emergency

No internet? Dial *384*MAMA# on any phone to trigger the same alert by USSD.

Who gets alerted instantly

🚐
Nearest transport
Ambulance or registered m-mama community driver, with your GPS location

👨‍👩‍👧
Family contacts
Up to 3 people you chose, by SMS

💡 Emergency care is a right — even without insurance

Under Kenya's Social Health Authority (SHA), emergency, chronic & critical care via the ECCIF is meant to be accessible without upfront premiums. Maternal Support Network shows your nearest facilities and flags this so cost never stops you seeking emergency help. Confirm current local procedures with your facility.

Guidance

Start timing when a contraction begins. The "5-1-1" guide many nurses use: contractions about 5 minutes apart, each lasting 1 minute, continuing for 1 hour — that often means it's time to head to the facility. Always follow your own midwife's advice first.

⚠️ This timer is a guide, not a diagnosis. If you notice any danger sign — bleeding, severe headache, blurred vision, convulsions, reduced baby movement — use Emergency Help now, regardless of the timer.

Financial preparedness · cost should never delay care

Financial Support

Lack of money for transport, supplies or an emergency is a leading reason care comes too late. Maternal Support Network helps you plan ahead and connects you to programmes you may not know you qualify for.

SHA / SHIF (formerly Linda Mama)
Government maternal cover — antenatal, delivery, postnatal. We help you register.

Join or link a group birth-savings plan.

⚠️ Maternal Support Network gives general guidance, not regulated financial or insurance advice. Confirm current SHA/SHIF benefits and tariffs with an official source before relying on them.

Pregnancy guide · clear, trusted, in your language

Pregnancy Guide

Short, practical lessons delivered by voice and SMS, paced to your weeks of pregnancy — co-developed with midwives and reviewed against Ministry of Health guidance.

🍲 Eating well

Iron-rich and varied meals, why anaemia matters, and affordable local foods that help you and your baby.

🩺 Antenatal visits

Why at least 8 contacts matter, what happens at each, and how Maternal Support Network reminds you.

💊 Medication & supplements

Iron, folate and how to take them safely. Never start new medicine without a provider.

🎒 Birth-preparedness plan

Your facility, transport, savings, and who travels with you — decided early, calmly.

🤱 After birth

Postnatal danger signs, breastfeeding, newborn care, and postnatal check-ups.

🧠 Your wellbeing

Rest, support, and recognising when you need extra help — including emotional support.

Live prototype · how an emergency is coordinated

Care Engine — Live Demo

An emergency flows through five coordinated agents: Listener takes the alert (voice/SMS/USSD) → Triage reads danger signs and urgency → Coordinator dispatches transport and care → Companion guides the mother and family → Recorder logs it for the midwife. Each agent is bounded by RANK, hands off via HUNT, watched by GUARD — with PRIDE-Loop human pauses on anything clinical.

RANK — bounded autonomy

Role · Authority · Notification · Kill Switch. The Companion can send reassurance and instructions on its own, but dispatching transport or giving any clinical advice requires a human midwife to confirm — and a USSD kill code pauses automation.

PRIDE Loop — human in the loop

Pause · Review · Interpretability · Disagreement rights · Elders council. No diagnosis is ever automated; a midwife confirms every clinical decision, and the mother can always reach a human.

Ethics & data charter · responsible by design

Ethics & Data Charter

A maternal-health system holds the most sensitive data a person has, in the most vulnerable moments. These frameworks — from the Safari curriculum — keep it safe, fair, sovereign and always under human medical oversight.

ETHOS — Empathy · Transparency · Human Impact · Ownership · Sovereignty. Who could be harmed by a missed or wrong alert; can a midwife trace why guidance was given; what a delay means for mother and baby; who is clinically accountable; whose data and dignity we protect.
TRACK — Training data · Representation · Amplification · Counterfactuals · Kill Switch. Guards against advice that works for urban mothers but fails pastoralist ones; counterfactual checks across language and location; a kill-switch on any automated triage that drifts.
OASIS — Opt-in · Anonymization · Sovereignty · Intentional retention · Security. Consent in local language; health data stored in-country under the Kenya Data Protection Act 2019; encrypted; minimal retention; never sold. DPA 2019 · health-data sensitive
PRIDE Loop — Pause · Review · Interpretability · Disagreement rights · Elders council. Mandatory human (midwife/clinician) confirmation before any clinical action; explanations a CHW in a remote area can act on; a USSD route to a human; governance shared with midwives, mothers and community elders.
HORIZON Scan — Historical harm · Opportunity cost · Ripple effects · Intergenerational · Zero-sum · Open futures · Non-human stakeholders. Does the tool build trust in skilled care or quietly replace it? Does it widen or narrow equity across generations of mothers?
RANK · TRAIL · HUNT · GUARD · CYCLE — the agent layer: bounded autonomy, consent-respecting memory, coordinated handoffs, safety rails, and improvement only with a human clinical brake.
